chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out before the Fajr prayer (subuh), and with him was a piece of bread which he had dipped in milk, and he was eating while walking, and Bilal was calling the Adhan for prayer, so the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) prayed with the people.

key_terms.الْغَدَاةِ: The morning prayer (Fajr) or early morning time
key_terms.بِلَالٌ: Bilal ibn Rabah, the companion known for his voice in calling prayer
key_terms.كِسْرَةٌ: A piece or crumb of bread

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet eat and do before the morning prayer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him and his family) ease and lack of rigidity in daily habits, specifically consuming food while walking before the Fajr prayer. It serves as a foundational evidence (hujjah) in Shia jurisprudence for the permissibility of eating while walking, countering later cultural stigmas that viewed it as unrefined. The presence of Bilal calling the prayer underscores the seamless integration of mundane acts with the sacred rhythm of daily worship.
